name: Burrow or submerge
summary: The unit leaves the level the fight happens on, going under the ground or under water, and comes back up to act. While below it is hidden from everyone without a detector and out of reach of most weapons; in return it usually can't attack, moves slowly or not at all, and sees less. Coming up takes a moment and gives its position away, and it may have to stay up until its weapon has reloaded. Versions differ in whether it can travel below, whether one special attack works from below, and which ground it can dig into. The line with cloak: a cloaked unit attacks straight from hiding, while a burrower must come up before it acts. Digging in to harden a hull while still firing is deploy-siege-mode, and tunnel entrances that teammates share are build-linked-exits.
counterplay: Bring detection: a detector near the burrower shows it to the whole team, and in most versions anything that hits the ground can then hit it.
Scan likely hiding spots with an area reveal, or watch for the tell: ripples, dust or a shadow where it moves below.
Punish the surfacing: it can't fire while it comes up, so pre-aim the cracking ground and hit it before it can dive again.
Deny the ground: hard floors, paving and water keep the ground versions from digging in or coming up there, so hold the fight on them.
Force it up: in Tiberian Sun an EMP forces a tunnelling tank to the surface.
Spread out and keep moving near likely ambush spots, so one eruption can't catch a group.
Ignore it while it hides: a burrowed unit is not fighting, so take the objective while it waits below.

other_examples.note: One research lets almost every Zerg ground unit sink into the ground. Burrowed units can be targeted only near an enemy detector (or while a revealing spell holds them), most can't move, their sight shrinks, and going under takes a moment. Roaches with an upgrade tunnel about and heal faster below, infestors cast some spells from below, lurkers must burrow before they can attack at all, and banelings wait under the ground as living mines. Alert players spot a faint shimmer on the terrain, and unburrowing can fire by itself when enemy ground units come close. Unlike cloaked units, burrowed ones are not exposed by the ghost's EMP round.

other_examples.unit: Devil's Tongue flame tank and Subterranean APC (Nod)
other_examples.note: Nod's tunnelling vehicles travel unseen under the ground and break out next to their target: the flame tank to burn infantry and buildings, the APC to unload its five soldiers (often engineers) beside enemy structures. A deployed sensor array shows them on radar, an EMP forces the tank to the surface, and neither can dig in or come up through concrete paving, Tiberium fields or uneven ground (the manual adds water), so defenders pave their bases. On the surface the flame tank's armour is thin.

sources.title: Devil's Tongue (Tiberian Sun), Command & Conquer Wiki
Subterranean APC, Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Quotes the Tiberian Sun manual's paragraph on the APC.

other_examples.note: Both stay under water and come up to fire their torpedoes. Submerged, they don't show on radar and most weapons can't touch them, although torpedoes, the strongest base defences, terror drones and the big gun of the Allied assault destroyer still can. Coming up costs a short delay before the first shot, so fast boats often get away. The Akula's long-range special torpedoes are the exception: it launches those without surfacing.

For contrast (cloak rather than burrow): it stays submerged and invisible while it fights, coming up only when hit or when a ship comes too near, and only certain ships, sea creatures and other subs can find it. Its torpedoes can be seen, so attentive players can guess where it hides. The wiki notes that its Red Alert 3 successor, like the first game's submarine, has to come up to shoot, which is the line this file draws between the two patterns.

sources.title: Typhoon attack submarine, Command & Conquer Wiki

other_examples.note: Submarines and a few large ships have an order to dive and one to surface again. Underwater they can't be seen from above the surface or on radar, and only torpedoes and depth charges can target them, although sonar still finds them unless something hides them from it. Most attack subs come up to use a deck gun against hover and land targets, so the layer decides the weapon; one faction's sub can never surface. Some functions, such as a carrier's air staging, stop while it is under.

sources.title: T1 attack submarine, Supreme Commander Wiki

other_examples.note: After an upgrade, raveners spend energy to go under the ground, where only detectors see them. They move about a quarter slower below, and in Retribution they also pass under terrain obstacles and can't be knocked back. Coming up throws nearby enemies back, and in Retribution it also stuns enemy infantry for a few seconds, so the squad plays like jump troops that come up out of the earth rather than down from the sky. The ability has a cooldown.

sources.title: Dawn of War II/Burrow (Ravener Brood), Dawn of War Wiki
Retribution/Burrow (Ravener Brood), Dawn of War Wiki
Dawn of War II/Ravener Brood, Dawn of War Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: For one season, standing still for a few seconds on open sand sank a player into it. They then moved as a mound that threw up a sand cloud whenever it moved, gathering speed until it was quicker than running or driving. Firing, leaving the sand or reaching water ended it, and a short jump-out came before the next attack. Anyone could shoot the mound for normal damage, so it hid and sped a player up rather than protecting them.

shooter_analogues.unit: Swim form in your team's ink
shooter_analogues.note: Players switch at will to a squid and dive into ink of their own team's colour, where they swim fast, climb painted walls, slip through grates and refill their ink quickly; weapons are used in the humanoid form. Under the ink they leave only small ripples while moving and can't be seen at all when still; a gear ability hides most ripples at a small cost in swim speed. Enemy-coloured ink forces them back out of squid form, so each team paints the ground it can hide in.

A champion who switches between a surface form and a burrowed form, each with its own set of abilities. Burrowed, she moves faster, passes through units and sees less, and Tremor Sense shows enemies moving near her as rings on the ground, to her allies too. Unburrowing damages the enemies around her and throws the nearest one into the air, and ordering an attack while burrowed triggers it, so coming up is the ambush.

sources.title: Template:Data Rek'Sai/W (Burrow), League of Legends Wiki
Template:Data Rek'Sai/Unburrow, League of Legends Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: The upgrade adds a burrow: after a short delay the hero is underground, where it can't move or attack but is invisible, takes less damage and regains health and mana quickly, while its spells gain range and its carapace stuns nearby enemies at once. An unburrow button or its stealth ultimate brings it back up. A hidden, rooted caster rather than a traveller.

player_translation.summary: A hide-and-ambush tool for one player: on soft ground you dig in, then wait or crawl below as a faint ripple that only detectors uncover. You can't shoot or hold objectives from below, and coming up is a telegraphed moment that can knock back whoever stands over you.
as_user: Press Q on soft ground and you sink in over about a second; damage while digging cancels it, so it is a repositioning tool, not a panic button.
Below, your view shrinks, but nobody without a detector sees you and most weapons can't reach you. Depending on the variant you wait where you are or crawl at reduced speed.
You choose where to come up: behind a turret, under a backline healer, on a flank. Surfacing takes a short moment and you can't fire until you are up, so timing is the skill.
From below you can't capture or contest objectives, pick things up or use most abilities, so hiding never wins a point by itself.
A breath meter limits time under and refills on the surface, so you can't sit out the match below.
as_target: A moving burrower leaves a ripple or dust trail on the ground (in most variants nothing while it keeps still), and the ground cracks and rumbles a moment before it comes up.
Bring or call detection: a detector or a scan shows it to your whole team, and once it is shown the variant decides whether every weapon or only some can hit it.
Stand on hard floors such as paving, metal decks or shallow water: it can't come up through them.
When the ground cracks, step away or turn and fire: it is slow to act right after surfacing.
In some variants an EMP or a ground-shaking hit forces it to the surface.
teammates: A burrower waits at a choke while teammates lure enemies over it, then erupts as they push: a built-in ambush.
Its own team sees its outline below and its planned exit ping, so they can follow up the moment it comes up.
The other team needs at least one detector or scan; leaving detection out of the team is a counter-pick mistake.
With the tremor-sense variant, enemies moving near the burrower show up for its whole team, so it scouts while it waits.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; left mouse fires only on the surface.
Q: dig in on soft ground (a short hold that damage interrupts); Q again comes up where you are, or in the tunnelling variants at the cursor point within a short reach. One counted key.
Below, WASD crawls in the tunnelling variants, and the cursor shows a surfacing ring with the eruption area drawn on the ground.
With the automatic-dive variant there is no key: a moment after your weapon has reloaded and you stop firing, you sink again.
The universal keys work as on every unit, except that you can't enter seats or pick things up while below.
feedback: A ripple or dust trail on the ground where a burrower moves, seen by everyone and stronger at speed.
A cracking ground decal and a rumble a moment before it surfaces, with the eruption radius drawn on the ground.
Its team sees a team-coloured outline of the buried unit; the burrower sees a smaller, darker view, and with tremor sense the footsteps of moving enemies as rings.
A distinct outline and sound for both teams when a detector uncovers it, so a revealed burrower never looks like a surfaced one.
Floors that can't be dug are drawn with a clearly different texture, and the dig prompt greys out on them.
changes_from_rts: In the RTS a burrowed unit is simply invisible and untouchable until a detector arrives. Against people that reads as cheating, so here it always leaves a tell when it moves, surfacing is telegraphed, and every team can get some detection.
RTS units go under and come up on a click; here both take a moment and damage interrupts digging, so burrowing can't reset every fight.
The Red Alert submarine can stay under for ever; a breath meter or a forced surfacing after a while keeps players from hiding out the match.
No capturing, contesting or holding objectives from below.
The game has no naval class, so the submarine original becomes burrowing into soft ground (or diving into liquid surfaces), and its automatic dive becomes a variant.
Maps need soft and hard ground, so defenders can make safe zones the way Tiberian Sun bases were paved with concrete.

team_play.notes: The burrower's team builds ambushes around it: lure enemies over it, then follow up its eruption. The other team has to bring detection and hold hard ground, so both sides plan around it.

notes: Reuses the hidden-state and detection system that cloak, the stealth and detector sensor traits and disguise need anyway.
Needs a ground layer: soft and hard surfaces per map, and rules for where a unit may come up (never inside walls, vehicles or other units).
Visibility must be decided on the server: a hidden burrower's position is never sent to enemy clients until it is uncovered or shows its tell, or cheats will expose it.
Each weapon family needs a rule for what reaches a unit below, uncovered or not, and what EMP or ground-shaking hits do to it.
Edge cases: surfacing under a vehicle or a teammate, objectives and pickups, an attached infester, death while below, and drawing the tell readably at top-down scale.
A player nobody on the other team can find or hit is unbeatable, so detection must be easy for every team to get.
Escape abuse: burrowing out of every fight to heal (StarCraft II's roaches heal faster below) needs a dig time, a damage interrupt and a cooldown.
Hiding out the clock or stalling objectives; burrowed players stay out of objectives and time below is limited.
An eruption plus a first strike can delete fragile players with no window to react; keep surfacing telegraphed and the burst modest.
Tunnelling past every defence straight into the backline, as Tiberian Sun's subterranean units did, makes defence pointless unless key areas have hard floors.
An unseen player is the hardest thing to read from a top-down camera; the ripple tell must be visible but subtle.
Players must know which ground can be dug and which weapons hit a burrower once it is uncovered.
Its own team must see where it is, or they will stand on its exit and block the ambush.
A detected burrower must look different from one that has surfaced.

variants.name: Dig in and wait
variants.summary: You go under where you stand and can't move or attack until you come up, but nobody without a detector can see or reach you.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft zerg Burrow, Dota 2 Nyx Assassin

variants.name: Tunnel
variants.summary: You crawl below at reduced speed, unseen except for a faint ripple, and come up anywhere the ground allows, including past walls the surface route must go round.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II roaches with Tunneling Claws, Dawn of War II raveners, Tiberian Sun Devil's Tongue

variants.name: Shallow mound
variants.summary: You travel just under the surface as a mound that is faster than running and blends into the ground, but anyone can shoot the mound, and firing means jumping out first.

adds_strengths.why: Below the surface it moves faster than running and is easy to miss among cover and props.

adds_weaknesses.why: The mound can be shot like any target and throws up dust as it moves, and it must jump out before it can attack.

variants.name: Erupting ambush
variants.summary: Coming up knocks the enemies around you back or up (a brief stun only from T2 up), and ordering an attack on a nearby enemy from below surfaces you with the knock-up on it.
variants.seen_in: Dawn of War II raveners, League of Legends Rek'Sai

counters.why: It comes up under soldiers without a detector and knocks them about before they can react.

variants.name: Tripwire ambush
variants.summary: You wait buried on a spot; when an enemy comes close you surface by yourself, with the eruption if you have it, so you can guard a route while watching the map.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II automatic unburrow and banelings buried as mines

variants.name: Automatic dive
variants.summary: No key: you are below whenever you are not attacking, come up by yourself to fire, and stay up until your weapon has reloaded; taking damage brings you up too.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert submarine, Red Alert 3 Akula and Yari

adds_strengths.why: Hidden and out of reach whenever it is not firing, with no key to press.

adds_weaknesses.why: Every attack brings it up and it stays up until its weapon reloads, so each shot gives its position away.

variants.name: Strike from below
variants.summary: One attack works from below without surfacing, such as a line of spikes through the ground or a long-range charge on a cooldown; using it shows your position for a moment.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft lurkers, Red Alert 3 Akula's special torpedoes, Dota 2 Nyx Assassin's burrowed spells

variants.name: Mend below
variants.summary: You regain health faster while buried and take less damage if you are found, so going under is also a way to recover.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II roaches, Dota 2 Nyx Assassin

variants.name: Tremor sense
variants.summary: Below, your own sight shrinks, but enemies moving near you show as rings on the ground for you and your team.

variants.name: Dive into your team's ground
variants.summary: You can only go under in ground your team has covered with a lingering coat (ink, foam, sludge); there you move fast, climb coated walls and refill ammo, and ground the other team has coated throws you back out.

adds_strengths.why: Below the surface it is hidden from everyone without a detector and out of reach of most weapons, so it chooses when and where to come up.

adds_weaknesses.why: It can't attack from below: it must come up first, which takes a moment and gives it away, and hard floors keep it from digging in.

counters.why: Turrets and other fixed defences can't see or reach it below, so it comes up inside their guard.

countered_by.why: A detector shows it to the whole team, and then most weapons that hit the ground can reach it.
A scan or placed sensor uncovers it wherever it waits.
An EMP drags it to the surface in the versions that use machines to tunnel.

open_questions: Once a detector uncovers a burrower, can every weapon that hits the ground reach it (StarCraft II) or only special ones such as depth charges and torpedoes (Red Alert, Supreme Commander)?
Should time below be limited by a breath meter, or should burrowing only hide and slow the unit?
Do Shamble Frontlines maps get soft and hard ground, so only some floors can be dug?
Is the ripple tell visible to everyone at any range, or only to enemies nearby?
Should every team have a cheap way to detect burrowers, such as a scan on a universal key, or should detection stay a counter-pick?

shooter_fit.reason: Splatoon and Fortnite show that diving under a surface works in team shooters, and ripples read well from above; but a hidden, untouchable player needs strict tells, easy detection and time limits.
